statement: Let T(A) be the finite nonempty ordered binary trees with leaves in A, generated by leaf(a) and node(L,R). A model M consists of a real u >= 0 and r: R -> R such that for every real z there exists a real delta with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Its operations are mul_M(a,b)=r(ab) and add_M(a,b)=r(a+b). Tree.map transforms each leaf and preserves all nodes. Depth is 0 at a leaf and 1+max(depth(L),depth(R)) at a node. For real-labelled trees, exactSum is the leaf value at a leaf and the sum of the two recursive results at a node. roundedSum_M is the leaf value at a leaf and r applied to the sum of the two recursive results at a node. For any real bound b, IsPerturbation(b,S,P) means the trees have the same ordered shape and every corresponding pair of real leaf values x,y satisfies |y-x| <= b|x|; its constructors are precisely this leaf condition and the componentwise node rule. For k in N and v in R, gamma(k,v)=kv/(1-kv), casting k to R. The constructions replace pair-valued leaves (a,b) by ab or r(ab), and roundedDotProduct combines the latter using a rounded addition at each internal node. The main target asserts that, if (depth(t)+1)u < 1, this computed real value is the exact sum of a tree whose leaves perturb the exact leaf products by at most gamma(depth(t)+1,u) in relative absolute error. The remaining targets state the defining equalities for the leaf operations and tree transformation and the u-relative perturbation property of the rounded product leaves.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: For every model M and every t in T(R x R), put u=u(M), r=round(M), and d=depth(t). If (d+1)u < 1, then there exists P in T(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u),exactProductTree(t),P) and exactSum(P)=roundedDotProduct(M,t). Explicitly, P has the same ordered shape as t, and each leaf (a,b) of t corresponds to a leaf p of P satisfying |p-ab| <= ((d+1)u/(1-(d+1)u))|ab|. The ordinary sum of these p equals the value obtained by rounding each leaf product and each internal addition according to t. The natural d+1 is cast to R in the inequality and quotient, whose denominator is positive under the hypothesis. No balance or sign hypothesis on t is present.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTerm.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model M and all real x,y, roundedProductTerm(M,x,y)=mul_M(x,y). By the supplied multiplication definition, this equals round(M)(xy). This identifies the operation applied at each leaf by roundedProductTree. There is no additional hypothesis.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model M and every t in T(R x R), roundedProductTree(M,t)=Tree.map((a,b) -> roundedProductTerm(M,a,b),t). Thus every leaf (a,b) becomes the leaf round(M)(ab), and every internal node is preserved. There is no additional hypothesis.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree_isPerturbation
targets.statement: For every model M and every t in T(R x R), IsPerturbation(u(M),exactProductTree(t),roundedProductTree(M,t)). Equivalently, these constructed trees have the same ordered shape and at each corresponding input leaf (a,b), |round(M)(ab)-ab| <= u(M)|ab|. This bounds the product leaves before the internal rounded additions used by roundedDotProduct. No depth or smallness hypothesis is imposed.

targets.name: Research.FloatingPoint.Model.mul.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model M and all real a,b, mul_M(a,b)=round(M)(ab), where ab is the exact real product. This is the multiplication operation used by roundedProductTerm and hence by the leaf transformation in roundedProductTree. There is no additional hypothesis.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function T(R x R) -> T(R), defined for every t by exactProductTree(t)=Tree.map((a,b) -> ab,t). A leaf (a,b) becomes the real leaf ab, while a node becomes a node of the recursively transformed children. It preserves shape and does not multiply subtree values together. Its leaves are the reference values for both perturbation targets.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: A function Model -> T(R x R) -> R, defined by roundedDotProduct(M,t)=roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,t)). With r=round(M), its value at leaf(a,b) is r(ab), and its value at node(L,R) is r(roundedDotProduct(M,L)+roundedDotProduct(M,R)). It applies r once per leaf product and once per internal addition; the input tree specifies the grouping. The main target represents this actual computed real value as exactSum(P) for a perturbation of exactProductTree(t), under its depth-dependent smallness hypothesis.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: A function Model -> T(R x R) -> T(R), defined by roundedProductTree(M,t)=Tree.map((a,b) -> roundedProductTerm(M,a,b),t), where roundedProductTerm(M,a,b)=mul_M(a,b)=round(M)(ab). It replaces each leaf independently and preserves every internal node without aggregating subtree values. One target states this defining equality and another bounds its leafwise perturbation relative to exactProductTree(t) by u(M). It supplies the intermediate tree summed by roundedDotProduct.

assumptions: All model quantifiers range over the supplied Model type. Its data include u in R with 0 <= u and a function r: R -> R satisfying: for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Delta may depend on z. No additional model properties are supplied.

All input trees are arbitrary finite nonempty ordered binary trees whose leaves are pairs of real numbers; the existential perturbed tree has real leaves. Arithmetic has domain R. No balance, nonzero-input, positivity-of-input, or representability hypotheses are present.
Only roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation has the extra premise (depth(t)+1)u(M) < 1. The other four targets have no premises beyond their domains and the conditions built into the model.

The perturbation inequalities concern the exact product at each leaf, rather than separate perturbations of its two factors. A zero exact product forces the corresponding perturbed leaf to be zero. The main target asserts existence of perturbed product values, without specifying perturbed input-factor pairs.
